summary:
TRAJECTIQ is an interactive, browser-based space mission design game that helps students and space enthusiasts experience the engineering decisions behind spacecraft missions. Built for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, it turns mission planning into a playable cycle: choose a scientific objective, design a spacecraft in a 3D hangar, balance mass, power, propulsion, budget, data storage, communications, and time, then simulate the mission and learn from the results.

Across ten scenarios and eight destinations—including Earth, the Moon, Mars, and Europa—players explore NASA/JPL reference data through transparent, simplified physics models. They respond to mission crises, collaborate in a four-person shared-device crew, and compare redesigned missions. TRAJECTIQ’s distinctive innovation is a deterministic decision-replay system that evaluates alternative choices from the same mission state and explains why outcomes differ.

With offline-capable gameplay, a simulation-grounded assistant, multilingual interface options, and 2D visual fallbacks, TRAJECTIQ makes systems engineering approachable through evidence-based experimentation rather than trial and error alone.
details:
TRAJECTIQ — Design, Simulate, Learn, Redesign

What is TRAJECTIQ?

TRAJECTIQ is an interactive, browser-based space mission design and simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms complex spacecraft engineering concepts into an engaging educational experience, allowing users to design missions, make engineering decisions, simulate their consequences, and improve their spacecraft through experimentation.

How Does It Work?

Players select from ten mission scenarios across eight celestial destinations: Earth, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Vesta, Ceres, and Europa.

The experience follows five stages:

  1. Mission Planning: Choose a scientific objective, destination, difficulty level, budget, and mission constraints.
  2. Spacecraft Design: Build and customize a spacecraft using an interactive 3D hangar. Configure scientific instruments, propulsion, power systems, communication equipment, data storage, launch vehicles, and orbital parameters.
  3. Engineering Validation: Monitor spacecraft mass, power availability, propellant reserves, scientific capacity, budget, communication limitations, and mission schedules.
  4. Mission Simulation: Launch and operate the spacecraft using a deterministic simulation engine. Respond to operational challenges such as eclipses, power shortages, communication interruptions, dust storms, and radiation events.
  5. Mission Analysis: Evaluate mission performance, scientific value, resource efficiency, decision quality, and collaboration. Redesign the spacecraft and compare outcomes.

Our Key Innovation

Unlike conventional space games, TRAJECTIQ incorporates a causal decision-replay system that evaluates alternative decisions from the same simulation state. Instead of simply telling players whether they succeeded or failed, it demonstrates why different engineering decisions produce different outcomes.

A contextual mission assistant provides explanations grounded in simulation calculations and mission data.

NASA Data Integration

TRAJECTIQ incorporates curated NASA/JPL scientific references, including planetary radii, gravitational parameters, solar irradiance, planetary distances, and historical spacecraft specifications.

Its simulation uses established first-order engineering equations, including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, circular-orbit calculations, eclipse geometry, energy accounting, and simplified communications modeling.

Verified scientific data is distinguished from fictional gameplay assumptions. TRAJECTIQ is an educational simulation, not professional flight-planning software.

Collaboration and Accessibility

TRAJECTIQ supports solo gameplay, sandbox experimentation, and shared-device crew mode for up to four participants. Crew members assume specialized roles, review spacecraft readiness, make recommendations, and participate in mission decisions.

The application includes responsive interfaces, interactive 3D planetary visualization, 2D fallbacks, reduced-motion support, offline-capable gameplay, and multilingual interface options, including Bengali.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber
  • State Management: Zustand
  • Animation: Motion
  • Simulation: Custom deterministic JavaScript physics engine
  • Testing: Vitest, React Testing Library, Node.js test suites
  • Deployment: Vercel
  • Scientific References: NASA, JPL, USGS

Challenges and Solutions

The primary challenge was making interconnected spacecraft engineering decisions scientifically meaningful without overwhelming beginners.

We addressed this through simplified but transparent physical models, real NASA/JPL reference values, interactive visual feedback, contextual explanations, and decision-replay analysis.

Other engineering challenges included maintaining consistent simulation outcomes, supporting multiple destinations, handling responsive 3D rendering, and ensuring the core experience remains available offline.

Impact and Future Vision

TRAJECTIQ aims to make aerospace engineering education more accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide. It encourages scientific reasoning, collaborative problem-solving, resource management, and systems thinking.

Future improvements include more advanced orbital modeling, additional missions, expanded accessibility, deeper multilingual learning support, and classroom-oriented assessments.

Live Demo: https://trajectiq-omega.vercel.app/
